findings.text: Provides four thin fill wrappers for copy with source, zero page without source, continue with barrier, and poison, each selecting its operation mode and delegating to a shared range fill core.

Shared fill core sanitizes alignment and span, resolves the covering mapping, offloads huge mappings to a dedicated huge path, otherwise walks the span unit by unit establishing middle level and handling each entry with periodic rescheduling.
Per entry dispatch chooses exactly one handler based on operation mode among continue, poison, copy and zero page, treating unknown modes as unsupported.

Huge fill rejects zero page mode, requires start and length aligned to the mapping page size, rechecks mapping type and page size after any retry lookup, and aborts when a concurrent mapping change is flagged.
Huge fill can release its locks to copy user data into an allocated folio when the table helper reports missing content, then clears the cached mapping and repeats lookup before resuming the walk.

Huge fill holds map changing read protection and mapping fill protection across the walk, and for each unit additionally holds a hashed fault mutex plus mapping read protection around table allocation and entry fill.
Outside continue mode, huge fill fails when the destination slot is already occupied by a regular entry, while marker entries are allowed to proceed.

Offers a single mapping write protection helper that gathers translation invalidations and applies a protection change over a clamped subrange, selecting set versus resolve behavior and optionally requesting writable upgrade.
Range write protection iterates overlapped mappings from the start, requires fault registration on each, enforces huge alignment where relevant, clamps to mapping bounds and stops on first failure.

Range read protection first scans every overlapped mapping for registration and huge alignment and only then applies changes in a second walk with shared invalidation gathering, so validation failure leaves no prefix modified.
Both protection range walks hold address space read protection together with map changing read protection and abort with retry status when a concurrent change flag is set.
Stability requires both source and destination entries still equal their sampled values and the destination middle level still equals its sampled value.
Eligibility for batched move requires empty destination, present non zero source, a normal folio that is anonymous exclusive and not large, and successful non blocking folio lock acquisition.

Present move limits each batch to the current middle level extent, flushes cache, checks stability under both table locks, rejects large pinned or non exclusive folios, transfers ownership and index to the destination, preserves dirtiness and soft dirty state, reapplies fault markers when destination is registered, flushes translations for moved span and continues while next pair remains eligible.

Swap move relocates swap state with cache consistency checks and soft dirty and marker handling, while zero move clears source with flush and installs a shared zero entry with marker handling, both gated on stability under both table locks.

Page move establishes a clear notifier range, maps both tables without blocking, rejects missing tables and transparent huge middle levels, rejects occupied destination and missing source unless holes allowed, pins and locks the source folio with unmap and blocking retry, and splits large folios before proceeding.

Fill and move loops advance by one unit per success, accumulate a byte count, convert pending fatal signals into interrupted status after progress, and report the count when positive in preference to the trailing status.
The fragments distinguish fill operation selectors named MFILL_ATOMIC_COPY and MFILL_ATOMIC_ZEROPAGE and MFILL_ATOMIC_CONTINUE and MFILL_ATOMIC_POISON.

Additional selectors observed are UFFDIO_MOVE_MODE_ALLOW_SRC_HOLES for moves and MM_CP_UFFD_WP with MM_CP_UFFD_WP_RESOLVE and MM_CP_UFFD_RWP with MM_CP_UFFD_RWP_RESOLVE and MM_CP_TRY_CHANGE_WRITABLE for protection changes.

Folio references acquired during fill and move are released on exit, table held references allow dropping the initial extra reference, and locked folios are unlocked on every completion or failure path.
